task.title: [Bug] rollingUpdatePartition panics when live StatefulSet replicas sit far below the desired count
task.body:
### Checklist

- [x] 1. I have searched related issues but cannot get the expected help.
- [x] 2. The bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] 3. Please note that if the bug-related issue you submitted lacks corresponding environment info and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be challenging for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, reducing the likelihood of receiving feedback.
- [x] 4. If the issue you raised is not a bug but a question, please raise a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions/new/choose Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] 5. Please use English, otherwise it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

`rollingUpdatePartition` indexes `states` past the end of the slice when the live StatefulSet replica count is lower than the role's desired count by more than `maxUnavailable` plus the number of continuously ready replicas. The panic is recovered by controller-runtime, so that reconcile produces no result and the workload does not converge.

This is pre-existing on `main`. It is not introduced by the error-preserving fix in #540. That fix removes one way to reach the bad count, a failed rollout read writing `spec.replicas: 0` (#539), but any other shrink of the live StatefulSet into the same range still panics.

#### Root cause

`getReplicaStates` sizes `states` by the live replica count:

```go
states := make([]replicaState, *sts.Spec.Replicas)
```

Case 6 then adjusts `rollingStep` with the gap between the burst size and the live count, and passes that step into `rollingUpdatePartition` together with the live count. After that adjustment the partition index no longer depends on the live count:

```text
rollingStepPartition = role.Replicas - continuousReadyReplicas - maxUnavailable
```

`continuousReadyReplicas` is the number of ready and updated replicas counted from the tail of `states`. The first loop then reads `states[idx]` for every `idx < rollingStepPartition`:

```go
for idx := 0; idx < int(rollingStepPartition); idx++ {
    if !states[idx].ready {
        unavailable++
    }
}
```

The loop panics when `rollingStepPartition > len(states)`, that is when:

```text
liveReplicas < role.Replicas - continuousReadyReplicas - maxUnavailable
```

With `maxUnavailable: 1`, `maxSurge: 1`, desired replicas 4, and no continuously ready replica, a live count of 0 or 1 is enough. A completed rollout does not enter this path. The role-size annotation must still match `role.replicas`, so this is case 6 rather than the replica-change path.

#### Expected behavior

Return an error, or clamp the index to the live slice, and leave the existing StatefulSet specification unchanged so reconciliation can be retried.

#### Actual behavior

The reconcile panics with an index-out-of-range error. controller-runtime recovers it, and the StatefulSet is left at the shrunken replica count.

#### Suggested fix

Size the scan by `len(states)`, or return an error when the computed partition index is outside that slice. Add a regression test that calls `rollingUpdatePartition` with a live count far enough below the desired count and expects no panic.


### Reproduction

No cluster is required. `rollingUpdatePartition` is a pure function. From the repository root:

```bash
go test -mod=vendor ./pkg/reconciler \
  -run 'TestRollingUpdatePartitionPanicsWhenLiveReplicasFarBelowDesired' \
  -count=1 -v -timeout=60s
```

Save the following as `pkg/reconciler/rolling_update_partition_panic_repro_test.go`.

```go
package reconciler

import (
	"context"
	"testing"
)

func TestRollingUpdatePartitionPanicsWhenLiveReplicasFarBelowDesired(t *testing.T) {
	defer func() {
		if recover() == nil {
			t.Fatal("expected an index-out-of-range panic")
		}
	}()

	// Desired replicas 4, maxUnavailable 1, no continuously ready replica.
	// Case 6 passes rollingStep -2 with a live count of 1, so the partition
	// index is 3 while states has length 1.
	states := make([]replicaState, 1)
	rollingUpdatePartition(context.Background(), states, 1, -2, 0)
}
```

The same numbers come from a role with `replicas: 4`, `maxUnavailable: 1`, and `maxSurge: 1` when `spec.replicas` on the live StatefulSet is 1, the role-size annotation is still `"4"`, and the rollout is not complete.



### Environment

- Affected upstream source: `sgl-project/rbg`, `main` at `3612013e6f779401831f5947dc124cc4313faddb`.
- Also present on `fix/sts-defer-error-preservation` at `8e07674132b6ae3a0a1336d3106d2b8e3b336c78`.
- Workload path: `StatefulSetReconciler.rollingUpdateParameters`, case 6, then `rollingUpdatePartition`.
- Model / SGLang runtime: not applicable. This panics in controller arithmetic and does not run a model server.
